key_insight: PsychFound is a psychiatry-specialized large language model—trained on expert knowledge and clinical records—that achieves clinical-grade performance and measurably improves diagnostic and treatment decisions when integrated into psychiatric workflows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between general-purpose LLMs and psychiatry-specific clinical needs by providing reliable, domain-informed decision support that addresses knowledge gaps, safety concerns, and workflow integration for clinicians.
method: Domain adaptation via fine-tuning on curated psychiatry resources: textbooks, guidelines, and de-identified clinical notes.
Clinician-in-the-loop instruction tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to align outputs with psychiatric best practices and safety constraints.
Rigorous evaluation with clinical benchmarks and real-world deployment tests measuring diagnostic accuracy, treatment recommendation quality, and clinician utility.
impact: Demonstrates that targeted domain adaptation plus clinician feedback can produce LLMs with clinical-grade utility, offering a reproducible path for developing specialty AI assistants and improving model safety, reliability, and adoption in healthcare settings.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: data sources (guidelines, notes) → training stages (fine-tune, RLHF) → deployment in clinic
Bar/line chart comparing PsychFound vs baseline LLMs on diagnostic accuracy, treatment concordance, and safety metrics
Clinical workflow illustration showing clinician queries, model suggestions, and decision feedback loop
Icon-based checklist of safety features and governance (de-identification, oversight, audit trails)
paper_title: A domain-adapted large language model to support clinicians in psychiatric clinical practice
paper_authors: Ruoxi Wang, Shuyu Liu, Ling Zhang, Xuequan Zhu, Zhi Yang
